To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NHE‐inhibitor cariporide improves LV remodeling and systolic and diastolic function in rats with heart‐failure induced by MI.
inhibition of NHE1 significantly improved LV remodeling in rats after MI, and that the effect was comparable or tended even to be stronger compared to ACE inhibition.
Inhibition of NHE‐ 1 with the selective inhibitor cariporid improved cardiac function and remodeling after MI.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of the Na+‐H+ exchanger inhibitor, cariporides, and the angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor, ramipril, on the left ventricular remodeling and function of rats with congestive failure induced by myocardium infarction.
the development and application of novel therapeutic approaches to the treatment of congestic heart failure.
the effects of combined inhibition of Na+‐H+ exchanger (NHE) and angiotensine converting enzyme (ACE) in rats with congested heart failure after myocardium infarction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of cariporid and ramipril was not superior to the monotherapys.
the combination of cariporid and ramipril may be superior to the monotherapists in rats with heartfailure.
the NHE‐inhibitor cariporide is effective in improving cardiac function in the rat model of MI‐induced congestive heart failure, but the effect was not superior to that of ACE‐inhibition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

inhibition of Na+‐H+ exchange by cariporide improves LV function and remodeling in a rat model of congestive heart disease after MI and that this effect may be enhanced by the addition of ACE inhibition by ramipril.
the NHE‐inhibitor cariporide has a comparable effect as ACE inhibition on cardiac remodeling and function in a model of congestive heart disease.
the combined long‐ term inhibition of NHE and ACE has a more pronounced effect than the monotherapie on systolic and diastolic function in rats with CHF induced by myocardial ischemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Na+–K+‐ATPase inhibitor cariporides has beneficial effects in the treatment of heart failure after myocardium infarction.

combined long‐term treatment with the NHE‐inhibitor cariporide plus ACE‐inhibition in rats with MI‐induced congestive heart failure had no significant additional beneficial effect compared to caripordide alone, but tended to be more beneficial on cardiac remodeling.
